headline: South Asia: Suicide blast targeting DI Khan police checkpost claims 12 lives, injures 30
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Suicide blast targeting DI Khan police checkpost claims 12 lives, injures 30.
- Persian Gulf Region: At least 10 people killed in Russian and Ukrainian attacks.
- Asia: Suicide bombing at police checkpoint in Pakistan kills at least 11.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Military personnel data exposed in breach, agency warns.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: Military personnel data exposed in breach, agency warns.
Unauthorized users accessed files containing the personal information of U.S. military personnel, a new breach notification letter warns.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: 8 sailors attempted suicide aboard ships from Lincoln strike group, Cao says.
Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao confirmed that eight sailors from the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group attempted suicide.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Bill blunder - Environmental levy bill withdrawn, replaced after certification cock-up.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: Bill blunder - Environmental levy bill withdrawn, replaced after certification cock-up.
Debate on a bill titled ‘The Environmental Levy Act 2026’ had to be suspended on Friday in the Senate and the proposed statute withdrawn and replaced as the document that was first before the Upper House was not a money bill. This cock-up triggered a stern warning from acting leader of opposition business, Professor Floyd Morris, who described the error as unfortunate. Lengthy presentations were made on the bill and the senators had taken lunch break to resume deliberations.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: It’s been an intense hurricane season in the Pacific.
Tropical storms have spawned in the Pacific in what seems like assembly-line fashion in recent weeks, as El Niño conditions that emerged in June have caused waters to grow warmer than normal, setting off a chain of unusual weather around much of the world. “It’s ramping up to be perhaps the strongest El Niño on record,” University of Miami hurricane expert Brian McNoldy said.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: Why AI has trouble predicting hurricane intensity.
THE CONVERSATION: Artificial intelligence (AI) has revolutionised weather forecasting in just a few years, with global AI weather models now able to produce forecasts that rival some of the world’s best physics-based prediction systems. This remarkable progress has been driven by three factors: massive amounts of weather data, advances in AI models, and unprecedented computational power. While most of the current discussion on improving AI for weather focuses on the models or new hardware, the data is crucial.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: ‘He was too great to stop at his death’ - JP Samuels Youth Foundation keeps legacy alive.
For Alex Ward, losing his best friend Jean-Pierre ‘JP’ Samuels felt like losing a brother and a purpose at the same time. Samuels died on September 29, 2025 with so much still ahead of him. The 25-year-old had just finished his master’s degree in corporate finance and was about to start working at a wealth management firm so he could support his mother when he suddenly took ill and died shortly after. But instead of letting his name fade, Ward and a group of Samuels’ closest friends turned their grief into action and launched the JP Samuels Youth Foundation.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

[Nile Post] On September 25, 2003, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi signed the Principles on Good-Neighbourly Relations and Cooperation at the United Nations Headquarters in New York, marking a diplomatic effort to end years of military intervention and proxy warfare in the Great Lakes region.
- Africanews, 21 hours ago: Macron and Pope Leo XIV unite on AI risks and nuclear weapons.
The French leader called on international oversight to ensure the most advanced systems mankind has ever created, are not controlled by a small number of powerful actors, or get used as instruments to oppress people.

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 18 hours ago: Namibia: Shafudah Praises Erongo's Coastal Beauty.
[New Era] Finance Minister Ericah Shafudah has praised the beauty of the Erongo coastline and the warmth of its people as Namibia welcomed delegates from across Africa to Swakopmund for the 9th Annual Conference of the African Network of Parliamentary Budget Offices (AN-PBOs).

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Suicide blast targeting DI Khan police checkpost claims 12 lives, injures 30.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Suicide blast targeting DI Khan police checkpost claims 12 lives, injures 30.
DERA ISMAIL KHAN: A dozen people lost their lives while 35 others were injured on Saturday when a vehicle laden with explosives was rammed into the Aman Mela police checkpost in Dera Ismail Khan’s Darazinda tehsil, officials said. Separately, two rescue workers were killed and another was injured when a Rescue 1122 ambulance came under fire while transporting bodies of victims from the blast. DI Khan Regional Police Officer (RPO) Ghulam Mubashir Maken, citing an initial assessment, confirmed the casualties from the blast.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: What comes after Riyadh meeting between the Pakistani, Saudi and Turkish military chiefs?.
The hurried meeting of the military chiefs of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye in Riyadh on Friday, followed by a separate meeting between Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman points to how quickly the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement is transitioning to an operational phase. The statements issued after the two meetings do not contain anything that would suggest that joint strikes or ground operations against Yemen’s Ansar Allah — commonly referred to as Houthis — are in the offing.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: Any attempt to divert Pakistan’s water to be treated as act of war, India ‘must make no mistake about it’: PM at UNGA.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday said that any attempt by India to divert Pakistan’s share of water would be treated as an “act of war”. “Any attempt to stop, impede or divert Pakistan’s share of the waters will be treated as an act of war. India must make no mistake about it,” he said during a speech at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York, where he called attention to the neighbouring country’s decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance.
- The Hindu - International, 5 hours ago: At least 7 dead as Russia, Ukraine exchange strikes and aerial war intensifies.

- South China Morning Post - China, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: Suicide bombing at police checkpoint in Pakistan kills at least 11.
A suicide bomber detonated an explosives-laden vehicle at a roadside police checkpoint in northwestern Pakistan on Saturday, killing at least 11 people and wounding about 30 others, officials said, in a sign of increasing violence in the region bordering Afghanistan. The attack occurred in Dera Ismail Khan, a district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, said Bilal Faizi, a spokesman for the provincial emergency service. For over two decades, Pakistan has waged countless counterterrorism campaigns against Taliban and Baloch insurgents in its western regions bordering Afghanistan and Iran, yet remains mired in a cycle of violence it cannot break. Scores of soldiers, policemen and civilians are killed every month in Pakistan’s northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and southwestern Balochistan provinces, where near-daily attacks on security personnel, government officials and other prominent figures are carried out by...
- South China Morning Post - China, Taipei Times, The Hindu - International, just now: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia test limits of Mecca regional security pact.
Just a month after Saudi Arabia signed a regional mutual defence deal with Pakistan and Turkey, attacks by Yemen’s Houthis against the kingdom’s energy infrastructure and military sites are testing the pact’s limits. At a hastily convened meeting of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement in Riyadh on Friday, military chiefs of the three parties reaffirmed their commitment to collective defence, according to the Saudi Press Agency. The agency said the talks focused on “intelligence cooperation,...

During their three-day summit that ended on Friday, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping worked overtime to underscore their increasingly close relationship even as the meeting produced few concrete deliverables. But the fact that the two economic and military giants are talking – and pledging to talk some more – suggests some period of relative stability ahead, certainly relative to last year’s all-out trade war, chest-thumping and market turmoil, said analysts, companies...

- NDTV - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: "Gonna Be A F***ing Bloodbath": How FBI Uncovered Plot To Attack Trump Event.
A group had allegedly intended to use drones carrying explosives to strike buildings near the fight venue, while a sniper team was to target crowds as they tried to flee.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 6 hours ago: Iran denies link to Houthi attacks; warns US as Trump rejects peace offer.
In a recent interview, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian firmly dismissed claims of Iran's involvement in the Houthi-Saudi conflict, highlighting the critical role of diplomacy in easing regional tensions. He condemned US and Israeli actions that exacerbate hostilities among Gulf nations and voiced scepticism regarding negotiations with Washington, referencing historical grievances. Iran's military also issued a stark warning regarding potential threats to US interests.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: 11 Killed, 30 Injured As Suicide Bomber Blows Up Vehicle At Checkpoint In Pak.
In a statement, the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan, also known as the Pakistani Taliban, has taken responsibility for the attack.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Woman lawyer from Assam assaulted in Delhi's Prasad Nagar.
A lawyer from Assam was reportedly attacked in Delhi amid a property dispute on Friday. Eyewitness accounts reveal that police were on-site as the confrontation unfolded, with a distressing video capturing her distress. The attackers expressed concerns about her being in Delhi due to the ongoing legal matter. In response, both parties have lodged mutual complaints, prompting several FIRs as police delve deeper into this assault and property dispute.
